cleared.check: Second independent line by line read of the 18 files of this unit: sign and direction of every delta, rounding direction of every math step, comparison operators, bounds on ticks, prices, fees and liquidity, unchecked blocks, casts and assembly.
cleared.result: I found no line in these files that lets a caller take funds or block a withdrawal for a token whose supply in base units is below 2^127. Amounts owed by a caller round up and amounts paid to a caller round down in SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta (signed versions at lines 261-288), in SwapMath.computeSwapStep (input with roundUp true at lines 66-68 and 100-102, output with roundUp false at lines 84-90) and in Position.update (floor at lines 93-96). The next price rounds toward less movement for an exact input and toward more movement for an exact output (SqrtPriceMath.sol:146-148, 175-177). Pool.swap debits the specified side and credits the calculated side with the signs the PoolManager expects (Pool.sol:371-382, 451-462), crosses a tick with the fee growth of the input currency taken from the running value (416-420) and negates liquidityNet only when moving left (424). updateTick and getFeeGrowthInside use the same convention for growth below a tick (535, 498-509). The per tick cap is checked only when liquidity is added (165-173), so it cannot block a removal. I could not compile or run the code because forge and solc are not installed, so this is a statement about the source text and about my transcription of it.

cleared.check: Solvency of the pool math under random use: can any sequence of liquidity adds, removals, swaps and donations leave a pool owing more than it received.
cleared.result: I transcribed FullMath, UnsafeMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap, LiquidityMath, Position and Pool into Python with 256 bit wrapping, separately from the transcription the accounting unit describes. I ran 28,000 random sequences of 5 to 60 operations with tick spacings 1, 10, 60, 200 and 32767 and one spacing above the allowed maximum (295757), starting prices over the whole tick range including the 2,000 ticks next to each end, LP fees from 0 to 1,000,000, protocol fees from 0 to 1000 per direction, exact input and exact output swaps of up to 2^120 units with near and far price limits, and donations. After every operation the price stayed in [MIN_SQRT_PRICE, MAX_SQRT_PRICE), slot0.tick equalled getTickAtSqrtPrice of the price or one less with the price exactly on that tick, and pool liquidity equalled the sum of the positions whose range contains slot0.tick. Every swap had a non positive input delta and a non negative output delta. At the end of every sequence all positions were withdrawn, every tick had zero gross liquidity, the bitmap was empty, and tokens received minus tokens paid out minus accrued protocol fees was zero or positive in both currencies. No sequence broke any of these checks. This is evidence about the transcription. It says nothing about what the compiler emits.

cleared.check: Properties of a single swap step with extreme inputs, and agreement of the source with the concrete values in the repository tests.
cleared.result: In 371,617 random calls of the transcribed computeSwapStep with prices over the whole range, liquidity from 0 to 2^128 - 1, amounts up to 2^255 - 1 and fees from 0 to 100 percent, the new price never passed the target, an exact input step never consumed more than the remaining amount, an exact output step never paid more than the remaining amount, a step that stopped short of the target consumed exactly the remaining amount, and the protocol share computed as in Pool.sol:391-393 never exceeded the step fee, so the unchecked subtraction at Pool.sol:395 cannot wrap. When the current price equals the target, line 60 infers zeroForOne for either direction, and both branches then return zero amounts, so the wrong direction flag has no effect. The transcription reproduces the nine concrete cases in test/libraries/SwapMath.t.sol:23-176, the rule of test_fuzz_getSqrtPriceTarget on 100,000 random inputs, the seven values in test/Tick.t.sol:115-160 for tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick, calculateSwapFee(1000, 3000) = 3997 from test/libraries/ProtocolFeeLibrary.t.sol:60 and getSqrtPriceAtTick(MIN_TICK + 1) = 4295343490 from test/libraries/TickMath.t.sol:79. In test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:129 the fuzz test expects InvalidFeeForExactOut for amountSpecified >= 0 at a 100 percent fee while Pool.sol:313 reverts only for amountSpecified > 0 and line 320 returns a zero delta for 0. I agree with the accounting unit that this case changes no state.

cleared.check: TickMath over the complete tick range, BitMath lookup tables and FullMath, computed from the constants as they stand in the source files.
cleared.result: I read the constants out of TickMath.sol and BitMath.sol with a script and ran the functions for every one of the 1,774,545 ticks. getSqrtPriceAtTick is strictly increasing over the whole range. getTickAtSqrtPrice(getSqrtPriceAtTick(t)) equals t for every t below MAX_TICK, and the price one unit lower maps to t - 1 for every t above MIN_TICK. getSqrtPriceAtTick(MIN_TICK) is 4295128739 and getSqrtPriceAtTick(MAX_TICK) is 1461446703485210103287273052203988822378723970342, which are the two declared bounds, and the threshold at line 36 is built from the same two numbers. getTickAtSqrtPrice rejects MIN_SQRT_PRICE - 1 and MAX_SQRT_PRICE and returns 887271 for MAX_SQRT_PRICE - 1. Each of the 20 multipliers at lines 80-100 is the nearest integer to 2^128 / sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i) in exact integer arithmetic, and the constant at line 225 is 2^64 / log2(sqrt(1.0001)) rounded to the nearest integer. mostSignificantBit and leastSignificantBit agree with a reference on every single bit value, on dense and sparse patterns for every bit index and on 200,000 random values. mulDiv agrees with exact integer division on 200,000 random triples of up to 256 bits each and reverts exactly when the result does not fit 256 bits or the denominator is zero. mulDivRoundingUp gave the exact ceiling on the same triples whenever it fits. The expressions of the form absTick & 0x2 != 0 depend on bitwise AND binding tighter than the comparison, which the Solidity 0.8.26 precedence table confirms.

cleared.check: Constants against their stated derivations: error selectors written as literals in assembly, transient slot constants read by TransientStateLibrary, masks, Slot0 offsets, the position hash layout and the fee constants.
cleared.result: With a keccak implementation written for this review and checked against known digests, the selectors match their signatures: PriceOverflow() 0xf5c787f1, NotEnoughLiquidity() 0x4323a555, InvalidPriceOrLiquidity() 0x4f2461b8, InvalidPrice() 0x00bfc921, TickMisaligned(int24,int24) 0xd4d8f3e6 and SafeCastOverflow() 0x93dafdf1. The four transient slots equal keccak256 of 'ReservesOf', 'Currency', 'Unlocked' and 'NonzeroDeltaCount' minus one, and TransientStateLibrary.currencyDelta hashes (target, currency) in the same order as CurrencyDelta._computeSlot. The 160 bit and 128 bit masks have the right width. Slot0 uses offsets 160, 184 and 208 with 24 bit masks, which matches the layout comment and StateLibrary.getSlot0. A byte level simulation of the four mstore calls in Position.calculatePositionKey gave the same hash as the packed encoding of owner, tickLower, tickUpper and salt for 2,000 random inputs including negative ticks. DYNAMIC_FEE_FLAG is bit 23, OVERRIDE_FEE_FLAG is bit 22, REMOVE_OVERRIDE_MASK clears only bit 22 and MAX_LP_FEE equals SwapMath.MAX_SWAP_FEE. The protocol fee thresholds are 1001 and 1001 << 12, so each direction is limited to 1000, and calculateSwapFee stays between the protocol fee and 1,000,000.

cleared.check: Whether the int128 casts on liquidity amounts and fees can stop a withdrawal for an ordinary token, and whether the fee cast revert reported by the accounting unit can be reached without paying 2^127 base units.
cleared.result: A removal whose amount in one currency is 2^127 or more reverts in toInt128 at Pool.sol:212-234. The amount scales with liquidityDelta, so the owner can remove the position in smaller parts. In the 28,000 fuzz sequences three final removals reverted for this reason (seeds 12742, 13908 and 111494, all at extreme prices), each succeeded after the liquidity delta was halved once, and every position was fully withdrawn. If principal plus fees overflows in the BalanceDelta addition at PoolManager.sol:171, a zero delta call collects the fees first. The remaining case is the fee amount itself at Pool.sol:192. Fee growth inside a range rises only while slot0.tick is inside the range, when the position's liquidity is part of pool liquidity, and each rise is floor(fee * 2^128 / liquidity) (Pool.sol:404-405, 474-477). The amount owed to a position is therefore at most the fees and donations actually paid while it was in range. A donor who also holds a large position in the same range gets back only that position's share, so the donor's net cost equals what the other positions are owed. Borrowing through take does not help, because the borrowed amount has to be repaid in the same unlock. The solvency check of the fuzz covers the same statement. The fee cast revert therefore needs 2^127 base units of one currency given up by payers, which is possible only for a token whose supply in base units exceeds 2^127 or whose balanceOf is under the attacker's control.

cleared.check: A9, gas caps against the loops in the pool math: can a block or transaction gas cap stop liquidity providers from withdrawing, on HyperEVM with 3,000,000 gas blocks in particular.
cleared.result: Pool.modifyLiquidity has no loop. It updates two ticks, at most two bitmap words, one position and the pool liquidity (Pool.sol:159-236). The repository's own gas snapshots, which I did not re-measure, record 130,613 gas for a removal with an empty hook, 161,276 for a simple add and 292,593 for a new salted position, all through test routers. These are far below the smallest cap in networks.json. On HyperEVM, 80 of the 81 blocks from 51,944,427 to 51,944,507 had a gas limit of 3,000,000 and one had 30,000,000, which agrees with the dual block documentation. The only loop is in Pool.swap (Pool.sol:344-437). It advances one bitmap word per step when no tick is initialized, and a pool with tick spacing 1 has 6,932 words across the whole tick range. The snapshots give about 2,250 gas for the bitmap lookup and 900 to 1,600 gas for computeSwapStep per step, and I did not measure getSqrtPriceAtTick or loop overhead, so a full traversal is in the tens of millions of gas. That exceeds a HyperEVM small block and probably the 16,777,216 gas transaction cap of EIP-7825 where that cap is active. I did not confirm on which of the 21 networks EIP-7825 is active. The loop ends when the price reaches the caller's limit (Pool.sol:344), so a long move can be split over several transactions, and no withdrawal depends on a swap. A gas cap can make large single transaction swaps fail. It cannot freeze liquidity through the code in these files.

cleared.check: A10, arithmetic opcode semantics on each network: do MULMOD, SDIV, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, the signed comparisons, KECCAK256, TSTORE, TLOAD, MCOPY and PUSH0 return what the math libraries assume.
cleared.result: I built 4,394 bytes of init code that evaluates 65 vectors and returns one marker word and the 65 results, and sent it with eth_call and no to address to the RPC endpoint of each of the 21 networks. Nothing is written by such a call. The vectors use the operand shapes of the libraries: mulmod by 2^256 - 1 and by a 200 bit modulus as in FullMath, mulmod, div and mod with a zero divisor, which UnsafeMath expects to return zero, sdiv and smod of -887272 by 60 as in TickBitmap.compress, signextend at byte 2 and byte 15 with dirty upper bits, sar by 8, 128, 255 and 256 of negative values, shl by 128, 255 and 256, shr by 32, 127 and 256, the byte table lookup of BitMath, slt and sgt, keccak256 over 64 bytes and over 58 bytes at an unaligned offset, tstore followed by tload of the Lock slot, tload of an unset slot, mcopy, push0, selfbalance against balance(address) and callvalue. Every endpoint returned the 66 words that a reference computed from the opcode definitions gives (keccak256 of the expected return data is 0xf220f7680c51a4806b0d0bfa134c73004328c4b4397485cd6fb5f9219d71a1a3). The check covers the node behind each public RPC endpoint at one block, 65 vectors and no gas costs. It does not show that a pool behaves the same on every network, and it does not test transient storage across calls or transactions.

cleared.check: StateLibrary and TransientStateLibrary: do the slots they compute match the storage the core writes, and can either library move funds.
cleared.result: Both libraries only call extsload and exttload, which are view functions, so they cannot change PoolManager state. The offsets 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 match the order of the fields of Pool.State (Pool.sol:83-91). getTickInfo and getTickLiquidity read liquidityGross from the low 128 bits and liquidityNet from the high 128 bits, which is how updateTick packs them (Pool.sol:547-556). The tick, bitmap and position slots hash the sign extended or bytes32 value before the mapping slot, as Solidity mappings do. getFeeGrowthInside repeats the three cases of Pool.getFeeGrowthInside with the same comparisons. POOLS_SLOT is 6. ProtocolFees declares two storage variables and ERC6909 three, so _pools is slot 6 if Owned declares exactly one. lib/solmate is an empty directory in this checkout, so I could not read Owned.sol and that link is unconfirmed. A wrong POOLS_SLOT would make periphery contracts that use this library read empty pools. It would not change core accounting.

cleared.check: Price range ends and exact tick boundaries in Pool.swap and Pool.modifyLiquidity.
cleared.result: A pool can be initialized at MIN_SQRT_PRICE, where the tick is MIN_TICK (Pool.sol:100-107, TickMath.sol:127). From that state every zeroForOne swap reverts, because the limit must be below the current price and above MIN_SQRT_PRICE (Pool.sol:323-330). oneForZero swaps and liquidity changes work, so nothing is locked. A swap cannot bring the price to MIN_SQRT_PRICE or MAX_SQRT_PRICE, because the step target is the nearer of the next tick price and the limit (SwapMath.sol:20-37) and the limit is strictly inside the bounds, so slot0.tick stays between MIN_TICK and MAX_TICK - 1 and the decrement at Pool.sol:431 never produces MIN_TICK - 1. About one third of the 28,000 fuzz sequences started within 2,000 ticks of an end, and the tick and price relation held after every operation.

leads.question: Does Owned.sol at the pinned solmate commit declare exactly one storage variable, so that _pools sits at slot 6 as StateLibrary.POOLS_SLOT assumes, and does the Unichain predeploy, whose bytecode length differs, keep the pools mapping at slot 6?
leads.why: The PositionManager, quoters and hooks read pool state through extsload at slots derived from POOLS_SLOT. If the layout differs they read empty or unrelated slots, which can misprice or block periphery operations even though core accounting is unchanged.

leads.question: With solc 0.8.26 and the foundry.toml settings available, do the repository fuzz tests for Pool, SwapMath, SqrtPriceMath, TickMath, TickBitmap, BitMath and FullMath pass on the compiled build, and does the compiled Pool.swap give the same deltas as the Python transcription on the 28,000 fuzz sequences?
leads.why: Both source reading units cleared the math from the text and from transcriptions. Neither could compile. A compiler or optimizer effect on the assembly blocks would not show in a transcription.

leads.question: eth_estimateGas priced the 4,394 byte probe creation at 22,573,027 gas on MegaETH against 536,325 on Ethereum and HyperEVM and 535,533 on Monad. What do a first liquidity add, which writes up to 11 new storage slots, and a removal cost under the MegaETH gas model, and does any per transaction limit apply to them?
leads.why: Liquidity removal is the exit path for LPs. If MegaETH prices or caps storage writes far above Ethereum, the gas bound used to clear A9 for the math files needs its own number on that network.

leads.question: How many initialized tick crossings and empty bitmap words of Pool.swap fit in a 3,000,000 gas HyperEVM small block, and do the routers and hooks deployed on HyperEVM split large swaps or send them to big blocks?
leads.why: A swap that must cross many ticks in one transaction, for example inside a liquidation or a hook, can fail on small blocks. This does not lock LP funds through core, and it can lock funds in contracts that depend on such a swap.

leads.question: Do the block producing clients of the 21 networks, as opposed to the public RPC nodes, return the same 66 probe words (one marker and 65 results), and does a wider differential test of MULMOD, SDIV, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND and SAR on random operands agree with the specification on Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc and HyperEVM?
leads.why: Pool prices and amounts depend on exact 256 bit arithmetic. The probe in this cycle covered one node per network and 65 vectors. A single differing opcode result in a custom interpreter or compiler backend would change swap amounts.
